main_text.p: rea recte, inquit noster Hippocrates, Aphorismo quinquagesimo nono, quartę Sectionis, tertianam exquisitam septenis circuitibus ad summum indicari. Quibus verbis aperte declarat bonus senex exquisitas tertianas non semper stato circuitu, sed interdum quarto, aut quinto, aut ad summū, septimo indicari. At uero si huius acuti morbi indicationis author effet ipsa Luna, utique nō diuersis periodis & circuitibus ipse indicaretur, sed semper uno eodemq; praefinito, motuiq; Lunę respondente. Etenim nihil Luna dubie poteft agere, sed certo ꝑ suo motu & lumine quandoquidem naturale est agens, quod necessario[?] in hæc inferiora agit. Deinde si acutos morbos indicaret Luna, eos semper plenilunio finiret, quando videlicet noştri corporis humores moueret. Tum enim suo lumine maiorem vim mouendi habet, quam interlunio, aut quadriis suis. At in cunctis crisibus, siue salubribus, siue grauib. humores moueri constat ipsis euacuationibus manifestis, quæ tum fiunt. page.notes: Pencil marks in the left margin (small u-like strokes) are handwriting and are left out. The word "motuiq;" is copied as printed and may be a printing error. "necessario" is partly obscured by a mark over the letters and is doubtful. The line-end "mor-" continues on the next page, where the catchword "bi," is printed.
